enhancements: Replay listener applies accepted-socket timeouts before HTTP header parsing, closes owned connections during bounded cleanup, and records only complete response writes and flushes.

Replay acceptance requires a fresh UUID nonce, exact actual installation/scope/accepted epoch and digest, request and response body hashes, the fresh launch time window, unchanged journal, and existing Dart/FFI/data/bundle checks.
Before first engine creation, a new per-process provider ledger records session/PID/start/runner nonce with a manual UUID fallback; atomic locked events are bounded by count and size.
Refused and released callbacks retain only public validated identity. Event persistence is required before returning key bytes; persistence failure is fatal.

Every full Dart launch validates and retains provider.json as a fifth raw report. Normal paid releases match process-current identity; effective free requires zero attempts; missing keys require refusals; a wrong 32-byte key may be released before the VM rejects it.

The inspected Flutter source difference is engine.version plus a unit-test assertion; this does not convert earlier compile evidence into current-pin runtime acceptance.

limitations: All platform runtime_acceptance fields are false. Focused unit/helper execution, kernel generation and typechecking do not certify a signed native application lifecycle.
The earlier 62-launch Mac run predates complete-write replay evidence and the fresh provider ledger; it cannot retrospectively prove the new delivery or zero/release oracles.

Old response captures use an independent nonce and an older accepted epoch. Rejection of an additional corrupted signature remains a combined control, not isolated epoch or signature verification; capture consistency is not local RSA verification.
The 59-test iOS combined suite overlaps the Mac fixture suite and iOS subsets. Test counts here are not a sum of unique checks.
